quick_english: For in the teaching of the revered scripture, there is no action separate from knowledge. Knowledge itself, when firmly established in that way, reaches the culmination of yoga.

Yoga is not different from action, and action is not different from yoga. The cognition that is firmly grounded in reality and brings the impressions of one's own mind to rest is what is called action.
In one's own mind there are latent impressions born from karma, impurity, and maya. The cognition that arises to calm those impressions is essentially of the nature of consciousness itself.

That same cognition, which rests upon the outer range of principles that give rise to the body, is action. And that very same cognition becomes yoga when it dissolves those principles back into consciousness.
Even in everyday life, when one thinks 'I am going', there is first just an inner flash. That same flash enters the body, the place, and the senses, and then it becomes the act of going.
Therefore, even what is called action is really nothing but knowledge. For that reason, it is right to say that knowledge alone brings liberation, and this has already been stated.
Liberation is nothing other than the unfolding of one's own true nature. And the self's true nature is nothing other than consciousness. The verse then turns to what comes next.
The powers of action and the rest are grounded in the nature of consciousness, because they cannot belong to anything unconscious, and no separate substrate for them can be established.
In the scripture of the Supreme Lord, the powers are not said to have any separate substrate, as if they were qualities in the manner taught by the followers of Kaṇāda.
If the powers of seeing, action, will, and so on were truly separate, then saying 'Shiva is one' would become mere words without any real basis.
For this reason, freedom is nothing but consciousness itself; and when examined closely, it is seen to unfold into many powers.
Since liberation is the self's own shining forth, there is no reason to think that merely knowing a cause and its effect will automatically bring liberation.
Although knowledge is sometimes described as the cause of liberation, that is not the primary way to understand their relation; so the objection raised earlier does not hold.
Action is by nature knowledge itself, but as it takes on a grosser form in the self, its variety becomes visible.
Within the path of action, the means are divided into inner and outer and then into many further kinds, so they become countless.
This also removes the doubt some wise people had, that because the means differ, liberation itself might differ.

quick_english: Those very qualities, called powers, are worshipped in various fitting forms so that one may become fully absorbed in that reality.

tokens.grounds: locates the discussion in that context
explains how powers are drawn in by the logic of invocation and proximity

quick_english: In that context, an unlimited power or even limited powers may be drawn in, according to the principle by which what is invoked becomes present, and according to nearness or distance.

tokens.grounds: draws a consequence from the previous verse
names fullness as a drawn-in attribute
names luminosity as a drawn-in attribute
names consciousness-nature as a drawn-in attribute
names Bhairava-nature as a drawn-in attribute
states that pervasiveness draws in all powers

quick_english: Because of its pervasiveness, that reality draws in all powers, along with fullness, luminosity, the nature of consciousness, and the state of being Bhairava.

tokens.grounds: contrasts Sadashiva and others with the fully pervasive reality
names what they can draw in
limits their drawing-in to the scope of their worship

quick_english: Sadashiva and the other principles below the highest, lacking full upward pervasion, can draw in powers only to the extent that their worship is near or far.

tokens.grounds: refers to the condition just described
connects to the classification of the path
characterizes it as involving conceptual differentiation
locates the teaching in this text
marks what has been taught here
states that it operates through conceptual counterparts

quick_english: In this condition, the path taught here is called the Shakta path: it is a conceptual course, because it works through distinctions and their counterparts.

tokens.grounds: describes one established in the nonconceptual path
specifies the full range of possible paths

quick_english: One who is established in the nonconceptual path, by whatever route they enter—from the earth principle up to Sadashiva—through that very route becomes Shiva.

tokens.grounds: describes the heart as illumined by the initial flash of that level
names the luminous field of awareness

quick_english: In a pure heart, illumined by the first flash of that level, awareness comes to recognize itself as supreme Shiva through that very opening.

tokens.grounds: defines the means as rooted in supreme will
identifies it as a mode of immersion
names the recipients of this teaching

quick_english: Thus, those who live close to the wise teacher know this good means, which partakes of supreme will-power, as the Shambhava immersion.

tokens.grounds: describes the contents as maya-shaped powers

quick_english: Now the Shakta mode is described: it works clearly through mind, intellect, thought, and ego-making, in a conceptual way, dealing with things like will that are, in reality, made of maya.
The Shakta mode works through identification and through the sequence of intention and determination; even though it is a means based in maya, at its end it becomes nonconceptual.

tokens.grounds: specifies the subject as the bound soul
classifies it as Shambhava in a limited sense
explains both its incompleteness and its flowering
describes its full unfolding when the defect is removed

quick_english: The nonconceptual state that appears in a bound soul is indeed called Shambhava, but it is incomplete because of the defect of the limited knower; when that defect falls away, it blossoms fully.

tokens.grounds: locates it in the Shakta mode
identifies the key experience of that level

quick_english: Thus, in the Shakta mode there is a conceptual level marked by the awareness of agency; even when that awareness is clear, it still involves contraction, as explained earlier.

tokens.grounds: continues the same line of thought
describes the practitioner oriented to dissolving contraction
refers to the same power or level
states its creative capacity when contraction dissolves
names the power as radiant in that state

quick_english: Likewise, for one who is intent on dissolving the whole mass of contraction, that power becomes radiant and can bring about the inner appearance of whatever is desired.

tokens.grounds: frames the objection as a question
asks whether conceptual cognition exists in the Anava means
locates the answer in that context
reclassifies it as belonging to another means
states the defining feature of the Anava means here

quick_english: One might ask whether conceptual cognition exists in the Anava means. The answer is that, as defined here, the Anava means is marked by the absence of utterance, so that kind of conceptual operation belongs to another means.

tokens.grounds: locates the contrast in the Shakta means
negates their presence there in that defining way
names the dual structure characteristic of the Shakta means
identifies power with the play of difference and nondifference

quick_english: Here the word utterance covers outward expression and related operations. These are not what define the Shakta means, because the Shakta means is characterized by the play of difference and nondifference, which is the very nature of power.

tokens.grounds: introduces the Anu as a defined term
links the Anu to difference and to the Anava means
names the means in this context

quick_english: The limited self is defined by clear difference, and the Anava means based on that works through conceptual thought and determination; yet at its culmination it becomes nonconceptual.

tokens.grounds: lists the lower faculties and the individual
poses the possibility of pervading Shiva
refers to the teaching under question

quick_english: An objection arises: how could intellect, mind, ego, and the individual self pervade Shiva, since they exist below him? How, then, can such a teaching be stated?
The answer is that, in reality, it is Shiva alone. Being self-luminous, he conceals his own nature and then appears again in that very form.

tokens.grounds: locates the teaching in dualistic texts
states that the point is established there too
identifies the agent as Shiva alone

quick_english: Even in dualistic scriptures such as the Matanga, this is clearly explained: the light that appears in the lower levels is the established manifestation of Shiva himself, who pervades downward.

tokens.grounds: gives the reason for the previous claim
extends the manifestation to lower faculties
states the appearance of the supreme

quick_english: For this reason, the supreme state shines even on the level of intellect and mind.

tokens.grounds: refers to the two immersions or means discussed
states that nothing is accomplished otherwise

quick_english: Both of these immersions indeed move toward the ocean of the nonconceptual, but without firm establishment in that state, nothing at all is accomplished.

tokens.grounds: states that the result in awareness does not differ
draws a conclusion and refers to the teacher's statement
asserts the primacy of conceptual construction in this context
states that this was hinted at

quick_english: One should not assume any difference in the fruit of awareness here; rather, it was indicated that conceptual construction has a primary role in this context.

tokens.grounds: states the basis of the argument
names the epistemic status in question
locates the claim in a particular doctrine
states that nonconceptual validity is reached through conceptual sequence

quick_english: Even in the view that makes validity depend on conceptual construction, the nonconceptual is still valid—but its validity is reached through the ordered sequence of those very concepts.

tokens.grounds: describes the initial state and method of one who does not know the jewel's truth
locates the attainment of the meansless non-conceptual state
names the one who knows the jewel

quick_english: One who does not know the truth of the jewel may first practice through the means of certainty; by attaining the meansless, non-conceptual state, that person is called a knower of the jewel.

tokens.grounds: identifies the means of non-difference stated here
describes the means whose nature is both difference and non-difference

quick_english: Here the means of non-difference is called śāmbhava, the means of both difference and non-difference is called śākta, and the means of difference is called āṇava.

tokens.grounds: specifies the knowledge in this context
qualifies knowledge as accompanied by means
names the full range of ritual action
states that action will be contained within knowledge

quick_english: In the end, within knowledge accompanied by means, the entire expanse of action will be included in a very clear form.

tokens.grounds: denies that action is a thing other than knowledge
gives the reason for assuming sequential form
states that sequential form is assumed

quick_english: Action is not something other than knowledge; it is knowledge that has taken on a sequential form through the force of means, and this was stated earlier as action.

tokens.grounds: identifies right knowledge as the sole cause of liberation
names the divisions of self, other, and so forth

quick_english: Right knowledge, abiding in both self and other, is the sole cause of liberation, because the divisions of self, other, and so on are nothing more than constructions.

tokens.grounds: describes the teacher as having the nature of unity's flashing forth
describes the teacher as one in nature

quick_english: Even when all things are equally constructed, a teacher whose nature is the flashing forth of unity is called one-natured, accomplished, and liberated.

tokens.grounds: sets the extent of the teacher's continuum
identifies the continuum as the teacher
describes the continuum as made of right knowledge
indicates liberation by one's own self

quick_english: As far as that continuum extends, it is declared to be the teacher; and because it is made of right knowledge, one is liberated by one's own self through it.

tokens.grounds: states that the knower carries the continuum across

quick_english: For that very reason the knower carries his own continuum across; this is well established by reason and scripture, because to that extent the sage is one.

tokens.grounds: introduces an objection in this context
states that they raise an objection
states the claim that liberation comes from knowledge

quick_english: Therefore some object here: if liberation comes from knowledge, how could initiation and other ritual actions bring about liberation?

tokens.grounds: proposes that action is of the nature of knowledge
refers to the one in whom knowledge is situated
states the expected effect of knowledge
raises the case of another person

quick_english: If action is of the nature of knowledge, the objectors ask whether knowledge liberates only where it is located and what happens in liberating another; but they are dismissed at the root, and the text turns to what others have established.

tokens.grounds: gives an analogy for the removing action

quick_english: Some say impurity is a substance, like a film over the eye, and initiation is the action that removes it, like applying collyrium.

tokens.grounds: characterizes the view as rejected by reason and scripture
refers to the real status of the bonds

quick_english: We will refute that view later, since it is condemned by reason and scripture, and we will also show the true status of impurity, māyā, and karma.

tokens.grounds: describes knowledge as operating through the three powers
locates the classification within that knowledge
names the lowest or last level
identifies the last as the root
orders the middle, higher, and first levels

quick_english: Thus, in the knowledge that operates through the means of the three powers, the last is the root, above it is the middle, and above that is the highest, first level.

tokens.grounds: points to a level beyond the previous ones
names this knowledge as unsurpassed and resting in the power of bliss

quick_english: Even beyond that is a supreme knowledge, free of means and the rest, resting in the power of bliss; here it is called the unsurpassed.

tokens.grounds: describes the supreme knowledge as self-luminous
names exalted beings for whom it is rare
states that its true presence is hard to attain

quick_english: That self-luminous knowledge, whose true presence is rare even for the lords of knowledge and others, is spoken of in the revered Siddha Tantra.

tokens.grounds: locates the indication in the eighteenth chapter
grounds the claim in a scriptural statement

quick_english: This is also clearly indicated in the Mālinī, in the eighteenth chapter, by the statement that it is not attained without the grace of Śaṅkara.

tokens.grounds: describes its fruit as accomplishment and liberation
describes the composition of the treatise
identifies the work as a teaching

quick_english: By this very teaching in the Mālinīvijayottara, the fourfold knowledge that brings the great rise of accomplishment and liberation is systematized by me in this teaching called the Tantrāloka.

tokens.grounds: describes the object before its form is unfolded
states its initial mode of appearance

quick_english: Here, whatever is reflected on, whether inwardly or outwardly, first shines forth with its form not yet unfolded.

tokens.grounds: describes the initial appearance as unopened
identifies doubt as arising from that manifestation

quick_english: That first manifestation appears with an unopened, indescribable form; doubt arises only when some form is determined, and not otherwise.

tokens.grounds: expresses the questioning form of doubt
identifies a determined part within the primary appearance
states that part is clearly determined
describes doubt as having properties like existence and non-existence not yet unfolded

quick_english: In the question 'what is this?', one part of the primary appearance is already well determined, while doubt remains because properties such as 'it is' or 'it is not' are not yet unfolded.

tokens.grounds: takes the word 'what' as the subject
denies an extra meaning beyond the object
describes the object as not yet opened in form
states that the word denotes the thing itself in that state

quick_english: The word 'what' does not reveal any additional meaning; it simply denotes the thing itself while its form remains unopened.

tokens.grounds: denies that this is the primary doubt
locates the process among multiple properties

quick_english: The doubt 'is it a post or a person?' is not the primary kind of doubt; it is really the arising of determination among many possible properties.

tokens.grounds: explains doubt from the non-unfolding of two reflectable forms
names the state again as doubt
states that the distinction is clear

quick_english: Again, doubt arises in the 'what' aspect because two forms that could be reflected on remain unopened; conceptual construction, by contrast, is clearly different.

tokens.grounds: identifies the first manifestation as that of an unopened nature
refers back to the first manifestation

quick_english: Therefore, the first manifestation of a being whose nature is not yet unfolded is here called indication, question, and indeed doubt.

tokens.quick_gloss: by the path of the unfolding of thus-unrevealed form and being
tokens.grounds: tathā, anudghāṭita, ākāra, bhāva, prasara, vartman

tokens.quick_gloss: the state of being a disciple

quick_english: As self-awareness expands along the path by which forms and beings that were not yet fully revealed come forth, it becomes the questioner and takes on the condition of the disciple.

tokens.quick_gloss: because of concealment whose nature is the certainty of inner reflective awareness
tokens.grounds: tathā, antar, parāmarśa, niścaya, ātman, tirohiti

tokens.quick_gloss: also sharing in the rise of withdrawal that arises immediately after expansion
tokens.grounds: prasara, anantara, udbhūta, saṃhāra, udaya, bhāgin

quick_english: Because the certainty of inner reflective awareness is then concealed, the questioner also partakes in the rise of withdrawal that comes immediately after expansion.

tokens.quick_gloss: with her form not yet opened

quick_english: To whatever extent there is a clearly manifest outward expansion in which her own form has not yet fully opened, to that same extent she is called the questioner.

tokens.quick_gloss: having the nature of question and answer
even in the roles of teacher and disciple this
for it is not ultimately real

quick_english: In this way, awakening itself takes the form of question and answer; so even in the roles of teacher and disciple, the difference of bodies is not ultimately real.

tokens.quick_gloss: because of being awareness, the many inner forms
as in the case of a grape, generally and specifically

quick_english: Because awareness is of the nature of awareness, it makes the many forms that abide within it appear outwardly, just as both the general and specific features of a grape are manifested.

tokens.quick_gloss: of what is fit for expectation of a particular aspect about to be manifested

quick_english: When some property is projected only in a general way, while a further specific aspect is still awaited, that general projection has the nature of doubt.

tokens.quick_gloss: from the inclination of the cognizing subject

quick_english: When the awaited specific aspect finally settles, determination arises; it comes from the inclination of the cognizing subject, and not in any other way, not even through countless imagined alternatives.

tokens.quick_gloss: because of skill in the forceful appropriation of its own nature

quick_english: Then, because of the skillful force with which that object is appropriated in its own nature, it opens up; and by that act arise determinations that follow upon its definition.

tokens.quick_gloss: by following upon the aspect of the property already determined
examination whose nature is indication and definition

quick_english: Because each newly determined aspect of a property becomes the basis for what follows, examination proceeds again and again in the form of indication and definition.

tokens.quick_gloss: in perception, inference, comparison, trustworthy testimony, and so on
the triad of indication, definition, and examination

quick_english: In perception, inference, comparison, trustworthy testimony, and the rest, the triad of indication, definition, and examination shines forth in the cognition of all living beings.
Indication is non-conceptual, definition is conceptual construction, and examination is a further series of conceptual constructions, even within direct perception.

tokens.quick_gloss: because of smoke it possesses fire, thus
is to be taken as definition
the network of knowledge of pervasion and so on

quick_english: Saying 'this is a mountain' is indication; saying 'it has fire because there is smoke' is definition; and the whole network of knowledge about pervasion and the like is examination.
This enunciation is like a cow; the remainder becomes a definition in examination.
Such an enunciation, with its own desire, defines the sacrifice command; agnishtoma and the remainder are examined.
The creation of a thing, tolerating unwanted parts, is called enunciation.
Then only does one discern; future creation, arranged timelessly, connects all time.
The creation of what will be created and withdrawal of the previously created part, when duty is declared, is called the mark of consciousness.
The examination resting from creation and withdrawal is said, with a mother-approved fixed limit.
First seeing, then middle, then vaikhari: these are para, para-apara, and apara-natured goddesses.
Desire and the three powers are declared; this practice is breathed and extended.
In the supreme teaching, question-answer nature has fivefold relation-nature.
As said in Ratnamala, all is other-art-natured: great interval, divine, mixed, and fifth.
The unity of distinct questioner and speaker is called relation, supremacy, full-unity manifesting.
By this very method another relation is sufficient, scripture-declared through fullness union.
Thus this consciousness-goddess is by nature always the breath of three enunciations and form of all scriptures.
There first enunciation has elder-younger distinction; knowledge-means and supreme third means are named.
Shakti-means, human-means, time-means, seventh, wheel-rise, space-path, principle-path, principle-distinction.
Kalā-path use, power-descent concealment, initiation beginning, conventional initiation, hereditary rite.
Object-procedure, subtle initiation, immediate transcendence, balance initiation, indirect, linga-removal consecration.
Final rite, shraddha arrangement, remainder conduct determination, linga worship, festival purification, occasion-caused.
Secret practice, mantra flood, mandala, seal rite, unification, entry into own nature, scripture union.
Future narration and scripture-authority determination; with seven added to thirty, the wise always...
Practicing daily rites, he becomes directly Bhairava; in thirty-seven, complete knowledge, he becomes Bhairava.
What wonder, even small ones attain Bhairava-state by sight; this previous enunciation is said, now follower.
In the knowledge section, enunciation of bharva in order; in the second section, means-distinction.
Universal consciousness reflection, recollection rise order, mantra nondifference in supreme means is distinguished.

tokens.quick_gloss: the true principle of the teacher
the non-applicability of the limbs of yoga
disregard for imagined worship and the like

quick_english: The refinement of conceptual thought, the principle of reasoning, the true nature of the teacher, the non-applicability of the limbs of yoga, and disregard for merely imagined worship and the like are treated here.

tokens.quick_gloss: the arising of the wheel of consciousness
the equal status of prohibition and injunction

quick_english: In the śākta approach, the arising of the wheel of consciousness, the true power of mantra, the real nature of recitation and related practices, and the equal standing of prohibition and injunction are discussed.

tokens.quick_gloss: the conscious nature of the utterance of the vital principle
characterized as the path of entry into the supreme principle
tokens.grounds: para, tattva, antaḥ, praveśa, patha, lakṣaṇa

quick_english: Meditation of the intellect, the conscious nature of the utterance of the vital principle, and utterance as the path of entry into the supreme principle are set forth here.

tokens.quick_gloss: the conceptualization of the moving day and night, transitions, and so on
tokens.grounds: cāra, māna, aho-rātra, saṃkrānti, ādi, vikalpana

quick_english: The instrument and the principle of the phonemes are explained, and in the individual approach there is also the conceptualization of the moving cycles of day and night, transitions, and the like.

tokens.quick_gloss: in the conceptualization of the path of time
in the arising of that wheel designated by the wheel-dividing mantras and vidyās
tokens.grounds: cakra, bhinna, mantra, vidyā, abhidhā, tad, cakra, udaya

quick_english: In the conceptualization of the path of time, there is the varied play of withdrawal and the arising of phonemes, as well as the arising of the wheel designated by the mantras and vidyās that divide that wheel.

tokens.quick_gloss: the summary and the correlation with the principles
in this account of the path of space
in the determination of the path of principles

quick_english: The measure of the worlds and their summary correlation with the principles are treated in the account of the path of space, and a corresponding pair is treated in the determination of the path of principles.

tokens.quick_gloss: and the relation of effect and cause
the explanation of the sequence of principles
the nature of reality, the classification of principles, and the explanation of waking and so on
tokens.grounds: vastu, dharma, tattva, vidhi, jāgrat, ādi, nirūpaṇa

quick_english: The relation of cause and effect, the explanation of the sequence of principles, the nature of reality, the classification of principles, and the explanation of waking and the other states are all treated here.

tokens.quick_gloss: the nature of kalā and the conceptualization of principles as one, three, five, and so on
tokens.grounds: kalā, svarūpa, eka, tri, pañca, ādi, tattva, kalpana

quick_english: In the division of the principles, the division of cognizing subjects is examined, along with the nature of kalā and the ways the principles are grouped as one, three, five, and so forth.

tokens.quick_gloss: the sequence of the divisions of phonemes
the explanation of the all-supporting power
to this extent is analyzed within the investigation of the paths beginning with kalā
tokens.grounds: kalā, ādi, adhvan, vicāra, antara, etāvat, pravivic

quick_english: The sequence of the divisions of the phonemes and the explanation of the all-supporting power are analyzed to this extent within the investigation of the paths beginning with kalā.

tokens.quick_gloss: the contemplation of non-difference, trembling, and laughter
but in the application of the paths

quick_english: In the application of the paths, the contemplation of non-difference, along with trembling and laughter, is treated, as well as the multiplication of impurities, their true nature, and the manifold variety of power.

tokens.quick_gloss: this much is the summary of what is to be said in the examination of the descent of power

quick_english: In the examination of the descent of power, the establishment of independence and the manifold variety of concealment are the topics summarized for discussion.

tokens.quick_gloss: the non-usefulness of departure from the body

quick_english: At the commencement of initiation, concealment is removed through knowledge, fullness is attained, and departure from the body is shown to be unnecessary.
In the examination of the student's fitness and related matters, the conception of places divided by location, the division of general nyāsa, the offering vessel, and their purpose are covered.
The fitness of materials, worship, outer-door worship, sequential entry, the nature of initiation, and the purification of body, breath, and so on are outlined.
The variety of special nyāsa, the special offering vessel, worship of the body, and nyāsa and worship on the paths of breath, intellect, and consciousness are described.
The superiority over other scriptural groups, worship of the wheel on all sides, taking possession of the site, the five cow products, and worship of the earth and Gaṇeśa are included.
Worship of the weapon mantra, the fire rite, consecration related to fire, oblations of satisfaction, preparation of the rice offering, and rites ending with the tooth-stick are treated.
The rite of Śiva's hand, preparation of the bed, rites relating to dreams, and the observances are summarized.
In the fifteenth chapter, on the rite of becoming an initiate, contemplation of the self of the maṇḍala and the elaboration of the offered victim are covered.
Satisfaction of the fire, illumination of one's own nature, the rite of nyāsa on the paths present in the student's body, and the variety of what is purified, the purifier, and so on are treated.
In the sixteenth chapter, the division of initiation, the supreme nyāsa, the purpose of the being of mantra, and the division of yojanikā and related matters are presented.
In the rite of the son's initiation, the preparation of the thread, purification of the principles, burning of the bonds, application, and the division of the paths are stated.
In the eighteenth chapter, called the abbreviated initiation, the absence of birth and the like and a very clear division of mantras are treated.
In the rite of immediate departure, inspection of kalā, nyāsa of the sword and the like, movement occurring in the body, and the rite of brahma-vidyā are taught.
In the twentieth chapter, the full subject to be explained will be consecration ending with the examination of qualification, and also the rite of the balance.

In the twenty-first chapter, the procedures to be explained are the rite of the dead and the living, the net, lordship over positions, the group of consecratory rites, and the examination of strength and weakness.
In the procedure for removing the mark, what must be clearly explained is hearing, permission, purification, the removal of sin, and the cutting off of doubt.

tokens.grounds: topic of testing and appointing the teacher
of the disciple's view or mind
sādhaka status in the initiation procedure

quick_english: The examination and appointment of the teacher, his vow, the removal of the disciple's understanding, its divisions, and the state of being a sādhaka in the rite of consecration—this much is to be covered.

tokens.grounds: the rite of consecration and its aim stated as this
in the twenty-fourth chapter named the final worship

quick_english: The qualified person, the consecration, and its purpose—this is what is to be explained and discussed in the twenty-fourth chapter, called the final worship.

tokens.grounds: through bestowing enjoyment and liberation in this context
in the section revealing the śrāddha rite

quick_english: In the twenty-fifth chapter, in the exposition of śrāddha, the purpose—granting enjoyment and liberation—and the procedure are made clear, and the topics are summarized.

tokens.grounds: topic of daily worship for remaining conduct

quick_english: The purpose of the remaining conduct, daily worship, the supreme worship on the altar, the nature of the liṅga in its many forms, and the explanation of the rosary are to be set forth.
The divisions of worship are to be explained in the revelation of liṅga worship, and then the division, purpose, and procedure of occasional rites.

tokens.grounds: topics of festivals and circle worship

quick_english: The divisions of festivals, their specifics, circle worship and its performance, and the purpose of worship on guru days and other special beginning and end days are to be explained.
The examination of death, the procedure for gatherings of yoginīs and others, the method of exposition, the method of hearing, and the procedure for guru worship are to be described.
In the twenty-eighth chapter, called the revelation of occasional rites, are established the division of the qualified practitioner and the sequence of the lineage of siddhas and their consorts.
In the twenty-ninth chapter are the procedures of worship and of the messenger, the sequence of the secret upaniṣad, initiation, consecration, and awakening.

In the thirtieth chapter, the nature of mantra and its power are explained. In the thirty-first, the division of the trident and lotus and the explanation of the sky, the swastika, and so on are to be set forth in detail.

tokens.grounds: chapter reference and mode of treatment

quick_english: These matters are to be explained in detail in the thirty-first chapter. In the thirty-second chapter are set forth the distinctions of quality and principality, their own nature, and the worship of their power.
The division of kalā is declared in the full revelation of the seals, because from the thirty-two principles up to Īśa it becomes clearly manifest there.
Since there is no separate division here, no additional topic is stated in this overview. Even so, that matter is treated because it is primary and must be known in the sequence of another section.

tokens.grounds: concludes the preceding outline of topics
gives the purpose of the outline
marks transition to the next section
names the next task: defining the topics

quick_english: Thus the method of enunciation has been declared for the sake of easy comprehension. Now, in examining its characteristics, they will be explained in due order.

tokens.grounds: defines the subject of the verse
identifies the powers constituting that nature
names the essence of the self
qualifies the greatness that is concealed
explains how the self appears bound
describes the varied nature of the teaching or reality
states that the meaning has been made manifest
locates the revelation in this work

quick_english: The self abides as partless consciousness-light, and its own nature is the host of powers of consciousness. It appears bound by concealing its own greatness, and its liberation comes through revealing its luminous nature. This manifold meaning has been briefly revealed here.

tokens.grounds: names the cause of distorted vision
states the effect of false knowledge
refers to what is seen under distortion
qualifies the defect as visual distortion
states the power of clear discernment
refers to the purified object of vision
names the doubt that is dispelled

quick_english: False knowledge produces defects of vision like a cataract, so that even what is pure seems to be a place of impurity. But when that cataract-like defect in vision is recognized and removed, how could any suspicion of impurity remain?

tokens.grounds: describes the overwhelming effect on people
depicts the power of phenomena over awareness
explains how beings captivate the heart
states the hiding of the self's heart
names the charge made against phenomena
turns the charge back on the speaker
criticizes the arrogance behind the judgment

quick_english: O host of beings, you forcibly seize people's hearts, make them dance with many gestures, conceal the heart of the self, and sport in that way. Whoever calls you insentient is himself insentient and poorly taught in thinking himself sensitive; I would even take his insentience as a kind of praise, since it suggests a likeness to you.

tokens.grounds: locates the qualification in this teaching context
describes the purified state of qualified teachers
states their eligibility for the task
specifies the domain of their authority
gives the reason for restricting authority
lists the harms of unqualified inquiry

quick_english: Here, teachers whose impurities have fallen away, who know the higher and the lower, and who are grounded in the true being of Shiva are authorized to undertake investigation. Without that qualification, inquiry is fruitless and leads only to hatred, blame, loss, and begging.
